claims.text: There is a statistically significant positive correlation between BDI-II depression scores and time spent on online social networking in high school students.
Average daily time spent on online social networking among high school student participants was 1.86 hours.

evidence.description: Statistically significant positive correlation (p<0.05, R=0.15) was found between BDI-II-II score and the time spent on social networking.
Average daily time spent on social networking was 1.86 h (SD=2.08 h).

methodologies.name: Anonymous Structured Questionnaire and BDI-II Assessment
methodologies.description: A total of 160 high school students were surveyed using an anonymous structured questionnaire and the Beck Depression Inventory - second edition (BDI-II) to collect behavioral and physical metrics.
conditions: Self-reported time on social networking and TV

limitations.text: The study design does not determine the causal nature of the relationship between online social networking and depression.

future_work.text: Additional research is required to determine the possible causal nature of the relationship between social networking and depression.
